title: Machine learning on health records flags patients at risk of cardiac amyloidosis
summary: Amylo-Detect uses 50 routine EHR parameters in 11,616 Vienna patients (388 with high-grade scintigraphy uptake, 3.0%) and reached an AUC of 0.93 in development, 0.91 in temporal validation and 0.91 externally at Essen (n = 1,521). It found 12 of 42 cases missed in routine care. The study is a retrospective preprint.
ai_technology: Machine-learning model (Amylo-Detect) on routine EHR parameters
organization: Medical University of Vienna, Vienna, Austria; University Hospital Essen, University of Duisburg-Essen, Essen, Germany

evidence.tested: Temporal and external hospital validation against risk scores and routine decisions.
evidence.unknown: Prospective benefit in earlier diagnosis and treatment; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A machine-learning model flagged at-risk patients for confirmatory scintigraphy.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from the review input and author affiliations from Crossref metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
